The URLs are constructed using predictable release patterns under the project's own domain, which is expected and safe for this context.

The `pkgver` is hardcoded as `0.4.0`, so no dynamic version resolution via `pkgver()` function or command substitution is performed. There is no code in the global scope or `pkgver()` function that would execute during sourcing of the PKGBUILD. Therefore, no remote code execution or data exfiltration can occur during the `makepkg --nobuild --nodeps --noprepare` or `makepkg --printsrcinfo` phases.

Checksums are provided for both architectures and are not set to 'SKIP', meaning the integrity of downloaded binaries will be verified. Even if they were skipped, that alone would not make the sourcing phase unsafe — but in this case, valid sha256sums are included. No dangerous operations (e.g., `curl|bash`, `eval`, or obfuscated downloads) occur at parse time.
</details>

<security_assessment>

<details>
The PKGBUILD file defines a package for `tailcat-bin`, a binary tool distributed via GitHub releases under the Tailscale organization. The sources are fetched directly from the official GitHub repository using HTTPS URLs that point to specific versioned release assets, which is a standard and secure practice. The package includes SHA-256 checksums for both aarch64 and x86_64 architectures, and they are properly specified — not set to 'SKIP' — ensuring integrity verification of the downloaded binaries.

The build process does not involve compilation; instead, it installs prebuilt binaries, which is expected for a `-bin` package. The `package()` function performs straightforward file installations: the binary is installed into `/usr/bin/`, the license into `/usr/share/licenses/`, and documentation into `/usr/share/doc/`. All operations are confined to the package directory (`$pkgdir`) and follow standard packaging practices. There are no network operations, dynamic downloads, obfuscated commands, or system modifications outside the scope of the package.

No dangerous functions (e.g., `eval`, `curl|bash`, base64 decoding of payloads) are present. The package does not modify system configuration, install hooks, or request elevated privileges. It depends only on `glibc`, which is minimal and expected for a binary executable. The metadata (url, license, description) matches the upstream project. All actions are consistent with legitimate AUR packaging of a signed, upstream-released binary.
</details>
